title: NKTDWO 200 Pcs Wooden Puzzle, Colorful Animal Shaped Charming Fox Puzzles for Adults and Kids, 13.78x7.48in Jigsaw Puzzles for Family Game Gift for Birthday Thanksgiving Chrismas (Medium, Purple Fox)
evidence_clause: The Good: - It comes in a very attractive little cardboard storage box - The plywood used is good quality and has a good feel in your hands - The plywood is sufficiently strong that it would be difficult to break any of the tabs without a tool or purposefully trying to snap them off - It is laser cut so all of the edges of the pieces are clean and smooth - It's a cat puzzle--who doesn't like a cat puzzle?
full_review_text: I really wanted to like this puzzle, but after spending 3 hours assembling it, I am frustrated and disappointed by what could have been a really terrific product, but instead it is a a very poor product overall. The Good: - It comes in a very attractive little cardboard storage box - The plywood used is good quality and has a good feel in your hands - The plywood is sufficiently strong that it would be difficult to break any of the tabs without a tool or purposefully trying to snap them off - It is laser cut so all of the edges of the pieces are clean and smooth - It's a cat puzzle--who doesn't like a cat puzzle? - The image/picture looks and feels like it very securely attached to the wooden pieces, so I believe the image will not rub or peel off over time - The patterns/textures and colors used in the image are pleasing pastels and reminiscent of fine fabric patterns - The border pieces all have a narrow tan band outlining the entire puzzle. It makes it fairly easy to separate out the border pieces and get started on the puzzle - There are quite a few cool cat-silhouette shaped pieces scattered around the interior of the puzzle--what a cool idea! The Bad - The cute box does not have a latch or simple button to hold it closed and keep the pieces from spilling out or getting lost - The pieces are way, way too small, and the little tabs and slots can be difficult to put together for young hands or old hands. A typical piece is 5/8" x 3/8"--measuring from the outside edge of a tab to the outside edge of a tab on the opposite side of the piece, or 1/2" x 1/4" without tabs--the tabs are 1/16" to 1/8" long. - While laser cut, the laser still has a width, and that width is *relatively* large based on the size of the pieces. What this means is that the pieces fit together *very* loosely with a lot of slop. Since the borders of the puzzle aren't straight, this makes it difficult to properly form the shape of the border. - The slop (or 'play') between pieces also means that the connected pieces come apart under the gentlest of nudges. This is the frustration, where you found and fit some pieces together, then your palm brushes over them while you grab another piece and the pieces come apart! So, you are constantly putting back together and having to push the connected pieces back to their proper position. - The slop also makes it difficult to fit the next piece in. For example, when you've filled in an area except for one or two pieces that belong in the middle of the area, when you then try to fit one of the middle pieces in with, say, pieces on 3 sides of the new piece, the tabs and slots won't line up and you have to gently adjust the other puzzle pieces trying to get everything to line up. Finally, you do it, and the piece slips in where it belongs. But, lo! You've moved the other puzzle pieces enough that they've now disconnected from other puzzle pieces! More work that you've done has been undone, and has to be redone! - The box says this puzzle is good for ages 6 and up. I have known a lot of 6 year olds over the years, and not one of them could do this puzzle, even with help from an adult. A ten year old would have trouble maintaining their patience for this puzzle and have a lot of trouble trying to manipulate these tiny pieces, tabs, and slots. I think this is more appropriate for 14+ due to the piece size, the colors and patterns on the image, and the micro-size of tabs and slots. - I also would not recommend this puzzle for elderly (eyesight , dexterity, patience, and pastel color issues), certainly not a dementia or cognitively impaired adult - The picture of the completed puzzle is miniature, perhaps 1/4 of the size of the completed puzzle. It is very difficult to discern the fine patterns of the puzzle pieces and determine from the picture where the piece might go. - It shouldn't take 4 hours for two people to put this puzzle together, but that was our result due to the puzzle constantly coming apart (and we were trying to be careful!!) and the difficulty matching patterns on pieces to the picture. Note that we got the medium size. There is a large size, which is about 20% larger, but also has 300 pieces (vs. 200 pieces for the medium). So, each piece is about the same size between the two puzzles sizes. So I believe that the slop and disconnection problems we experienced with the medium puzzle still is a problem with the large puzzle due to the way it is made. My Recommendations to the Manufacturer 1. Your wood choice and the method that you attach the image to the wood stock is great, don't cut corners or change it. This could be a real high-quality, great product with a few changes to your design choices. 2. Scale the puzzle up by 1.6 - 2 times. This will make everything larger: the pieces easier to work with, the designs easier to see, and the relative size of the kerf will diminish meaning the pieces will fit together better and more securely (less relative slop and I bet the pieces won't slide out once they've been connected). 3. Keep the piece count at 200--if you increase the piece count because the area of the puzzle was increased, then you'll be back at the same problems as this puzzle has: kerf is too big relative to the piece size, leading to sloppy, loose fitting pieces that come apart too easily. 3. Scale the guide picture up by 2 times. Sure, the picture will have to be folded to fit in the box, but at least the picture will be easily visible and usable. 4. Attach a small plastic button to the lid on the box so that the box will snap shut and keep the pieces secure. Or use some other simple latching mechanism that won't break or tear in a short period of time. This is so close to being a great, long lasting puzzle. Scale up the puzzle, keep the piece count the same, keep the puzzle shapes exactly the same proportion (so the tabs and slots also get proportionally larger), and this will be a winner! As the puzzle is manufactured now, the puzzle is too frustrating to be fun.

full_review_text: I’ve included a couple pictures for reference - one of the pendant and one of Sir Hammond the Handsome himself. So I actually really love this necklace! Cat and dog themed gifts are easy to come by but if your beloved companion is a less common beasty it can be hard to find items like this and I was really excited to find a hamster pendant. This little hamster shaped piece of metal with the little heart cut out detail and my big guy’s name engraved on it is adorable. A. Dor. A. ble. The overall shape of the pendant is spot on as well (that stubby little tail!) and It seems to be very sturdy. I truly do love it. So why the two stars? Well, first and foremost it’s completely overpriced. $35 for the pendant and a 16” necklace (which is like tiny choker size) puts the total cost at $50. I wasn’t really bothered by the price at first because its the only one like it I’ve found and I totally love it. However about 2-3 days into wearing it my neck and chest started itching terribly and a nice red rash developed everywhere the pendant and necklace touched my skin (I’m really sensitive to cheap metals). The pendant itself had also become very tarnished. normally I would return something with this many issues (particularly at this price point) but I really truly do love this necklace so I bought a new sterling silver chain on Amazon (which set me back like eight bucks) and polished the pendant to buff out the tarnished areas. In order to keep it from immediately tarnishing again and from further irritating my skin I used a thin coat of my clear gel nail polish (the kind that needs to be cured with a UV light) and this has kept it tarnish free ever since. So only two stars because at $50 I really shouldn’t have to go to such lengths just to be able to use an item as it’s intended. I’m stubborn though and I enjoy problem solving and I love my necklace enough that I was willing to put in the extra effort to keep it. I can’t really give it a higher rating though :(

title: Oltree | Cooperative Strategy Game for Teens and Adults | Ages 8+ | 2 to 4 Players | 60 Minutes
evidence_clause: We did not find it to be very well written and it made what is a fairly simple game into one that was more confusing than it needed to be.
full_review_text: My biggest complaint for this game is the rulebook. We did not find it to be very well written and it made what is a fairly simple game into one that was more confusing than it needed to be. There are how to play videos available online and I would recommend watching one to get at least an overview before slogging through the rules. It's not complicated, but again... the rulebook is not the best read. The game itself is not bad. The narrative aspect is the best part in my opinion but not as interesting as it could have been. The events tend to become repetitive. There are several decks of cards and you mix up a couple of them depending on what scenario you're doing to give a somewhat different experience for each scenario. Scenarios come in short, medium and long so you can pick an appropriate one for the time that you have to play. The production of the game is extremely nice. The screen printed meeples, cards and player boards are very nice. The insert is very cute but has one big failing in that you need to bag your cards/components otherwise they slide into the other compartments. This kind of defeats the purpose of the compartments. I wish I could give it a 3.5 but no half stars are allowed. So 5 stars for the components, 2 stars for the rulebook (ease of learning), and 3.5 for the gameplay itself.

full_review_text: As a huge poetry fan, this is genuinely one of the best poetry books I’ve EVER read. This was my first book by Shelby Leigh and it definitely will not be my last. Even within the first few pages, I probably said “wow” and “oof felt that” enough times to fill up a page of my own. There’s poems of different lengths split into four different parts (each representing a significant stage of healing imo) but even in a few short lines, Shelby was able to articulate so many common concepts & feelings amongst humans (such as grief, insecurities, identity, self-love, regret, forgiveness, etc) into words so hauntingly beautiful. I use the word ‘hauntingly’ in the best way possible— so many poems stuck with me, with more pages bookmarked than not. The recurring theme of mirrors, shattering, and reflections is so brilliant & beautifully reflected throughout the book (no pun intended lol). I also really like how there’s some pages with illustrations to visually match the mental image depicted through the captivating words of the poem. It’s hard to put down but I highly recommend taking your time to read & process each poem, especially the ones that resonate with you. I can’t recommend this book enough, especially if you struggle(d) with self-esteem, regrets, and the complexities of mental illnesses such as anxiety, depression, & eating disorders. Thank you, Shelby, for creating such a beautiful masterpiece that resonates so deeply. <3

title: NKTDWO 200 Pcs Wooden Puzzle, Colorful Animal Shaped Charming Fox Puzzles for Adults and Kids, 13.78x7.48in Jigsaw Puzzles for Family Game Gift for Birthday Thanksgiving Chrismas (Medium, Purple Fox)
evidence_clause: The Bad - The cute box does not have a latch or simple button to hold it closed and keep the pieces from spilling out or getting lost - The pieces are way, way too small, and the little tabs and slots can be difficult to put together for young hands or old hands.
full_review_text: I really wanted to like this puzzle, but after spending 3 hours assembling it, I am frustrated and disappointed by what could have been a really terrific product, but instead it is a a very poor product overall. The Good: - It comes in a very attractive little cardboard storage box - The plywood used is good quality and has a good feel in your hands - The plywood is sufficiently strong that it would be difficult to break any of the tabs without a tool or purposefully trying to snap them off - It is laser cut so all of the edges of the pieces are clean and smooth - It's a cat puzzle--who doesn't like a cat puzzle? - The image/picture looks and feels like it very securely attached to the wooden pieces, so I believe the image will not rub or peel off over time - The patterns/textures and colors used in the image are pleasing pastels and reminiscent of fine fabric patterns - The border pieces all have a narrow tan band outlining the entire puzzle. It makes it fairly easy to separate out the border pieces and get started on the puzzle - There are quite a few cool cat-silhouette shaped pieces scattered around the interior of the puzzle--what a cool idea! The Bad - The cute box does not have a latch or simple button to hold it closed and keep the pieces from spilling out or getting lost - The pieces are way, way too small, and the little tabs and slots can be difficult to put together for young hands or old hands. A typical piece is 5/8" x 3/8"--measuring from the outside edge of a tab to the outside edge of a tab on the opposite side of the piece, or 1/2" x 1/4" without tabs--the tabs are 1/16" to 1/8" long. - While laser cut, the laser still has a width, and that width is *relatively* large based on the size of the pieces. What this means is that the pieces fit together *very* loosely with a lot of slop. Since the borders of the puzzle aren't straight, this makes it difficult to properly form the shape of the border. - The slop (or 'play') between pieces also means that the connected pieces come apart under the gentlest of nudges. This is the frustration, where you found and fit some pieces together, then your palm brushes over them while you grab another piece and the pieces come apart! So, you are constantly putting back together and having to push the connected pieces back to their proper position. - The slop also makes it difficult to fit the next piece in. For example, when you've filled in an area except for one or two pieces that belong in the middle of the area, when you then try to fit one of the middle pieces in with, say, pieces on 3 sides of the new piece, the tabs and slots won't line up and you have to gently adjust the other puzzle pieces trying to get everything to line up. Finally, you do it, and the piece slips in where it belongs. But, lo! You've moved the other puzzle pieces enough that they've now disconnected from other puzzle pieces! More work that you've done has been undone, and has to be redone! - The box says this puzzle is good for ages 6 and up. I have known a lot of 6 year olds over the years, and not one of them could do this puzzle, even with help from an adult. A ten year old would have trouble maintaining their patience for this puzzle and have a lot of trouble trying to manipulate these tiny pieces, tabs, and slots. I think this is more appropriate for 14+ due to the piece size, the colors and patterns on the image, and the micro-size of tabs and slots. - I also would not recommend this puzzle for elderly (eyesight , dexterity, patience, and pastel color issues), certainly not a dementia or cognitively impaired adult - The picture of the completed puzzle is miniature, perhaps 1/4 of the size of the completed puzzle. It is very difficult to discern the fine patterns of the puzzle pieces and determine from the picture where the piece might go. - It shouldn't take 4 hours for two people to put this puzzle together, but that was our result due to the puzzle constantly coming apart (and we were trying to be careful!!) and the difficulty matching patterns on pieces to the picture. Note that we got the medium size. There is a large size, which is about 20% larger, but also has 300 pieces (vs. 200 pieces for the medium). So, each piece is about the same size between the two puzzles sizes. So I believe that the slop and disconnection problems we experienced with the medium puzzle still is a problem with the large puzzle due to the way it is made. My Recommendations to the Manufacturer 1. Your wood choice and the method that you attach the image to the wood stock is great, don't cut corners or change it. This could be a real high-quality, great product with a few changes to your design choices. 2. Scale the puzzle up by 1.6 - 2 times. This will make everything larger: the pieces easier to work with, the designs easier to see, and the relative size of the kerf will diminish meaning the pieces will fit together better and more securely (less relative slop and I bet the pieces won't slide out once they've been connected). 3. Keep the piece count at 200--if you increase the piece count because the area of the puzzle was increased, then you'll be back at the same problems as this puzzle has: kerf is too big relative to the piece size, leading to sloppy, loose fitting pieces that come apart too easily. 3. Scale the guide picture up by 2 times. Sure, the picture will have to be folded to fit in the box, but at least the picture will be easily visible and usable. 4. Attach a small plastic button to the lid on the box so that the box will snap shut and keep the pieces secure. Or use some other simple latching mechanism that won't break or tear in a short period of time. This is so close to being a great, long lasting puzzle. Scale up the puzzle, keep the piece count the same, keep the puzzle shapes exactly the same proportion (so the tabs and slots also get proportionally larger), and this will be a winner! As the puzzle is manufactured now, the puzzle is too frustrating to be fun.

title: Complete Entertaining Cookbook
evidence_clause: Is this cookbook worth the money?
full_review_text: Williams Sonoma: nostalgic and elegant (oh, yes, and the recipes are wonderful) Content: In a time of microwave cooking and instant pots, it was really nice to find this gem of a book, a book that transported me back to the bygone days of my youth (as my granny used to say, “Yes, I was born in the age of the Pharaohs” ) and to my grandmother’s elaborate dinner parties and elegant meals where the dining room was lit with candles and decorated with flowers , where the utensils were laid out in perfect order, where the napkins were folded into flower shapes…you get the idea. Okay, okay, okay…so I don’t actually entertain the way my grandmother did very often (where would I get the time or the money-people, lavish entertaining isn’t cheap!!!), I reserve that type of formal elegance and fine dining for special occasions and holidays, but it is really heart-warming to have a book that shows me exactly how to prepare special dishes for special occasions, how the set the table, how to serve my guest, and how to be a great hostess in general. And the recipes…oh, the recipes!!! Every recipe I tried turned out perfectly delicious. I am salivating right now while typing this review! I even went as far as to emulate the food presentation in the pictures (with the platters and decors I already owned, of course). I thought the recipes were rather well written, were not overly complicated, and did not require the reader to have extensive cooking experience cooking (although some cooking experience does make the recipes more accessible). With that being said, I do think that the absolute novice cook may struggle with some of the recipes in WS CB. (By novice, I mean a newbie to the kitchen who does not know what the difference between roasting braising is or know how to steam, boil, or blanch). For the absolute novice cook, I recommend the ATK series. Ingredients: Granted, some of the ingredients are not always present in a home pantry, but they are easily procured from most local grocers, butchers, and organic markets (Walmart even has a reasonable collection of the ingredients necessary for the realization of the recipes in this book). Presentation: Every recipe has a picture! Normally, that would not matter to me as I have over a hundred “picture-less” cookbooks, but for a “vintage cookbook” (from the 80s-early 00s) such as this, pictures are rather important as they show images of recipes with which we may no longer be familiar; to me, an image of a final product, especially if the last time I saw said product was when my grandmother made it in the 80s, is essential. The pictures themselves are breathtaking works of art, elegant, romantic (yes, romantic), and inspiring! The book itself is easy to handle (not too heavy, bulky, or big, but also not too small) and easy to read. The paper is thick and glossy. The font is dark enough and large enough to read, but I do use reading glasses (I am of an age where I simply cannot read ANYTHING without reading glasses. I have to have 16 point font on my computer to read without glasses). Simply put, the book is elegantly compiled and presented. Repetition: Yes, some of the recipes may be found in other editions of WS CBs, but to me that is of no concern as I am collecting ALL the WS CBs published in the 80s and 90s (well, anything prior to 2010 really). Delivery: arrived three days earlier than anticipated. Price: bought the used edition; copy cost me less than $5; pretty good deal! Condition: although I purchased the used edition, I got a copy in excellent condition. Conclusion: It is a product from WS. What is not to like? Is this cookbook worth the money? Should you buy it? For me, the answer to both questions is a resounding, unequivocal YES! As with all WS CBs, this is a beautiful book with elegant and tasty recipes, with lovely photographs of each described dish, and with side ideas and suggestions for improvement. Recommendation: Highly recommend! I cannot recommend this book enough even if I tired! I love it. Note: If you found this review helpful in some way, please click the helpful button. Thank you.

full_review_text: This was probably the first rock biography that I read. I bought it when it came out based on a review either in MM or NME. I was a big fan of the Who and at the time there were few first account books on a performer. The book was very fresh ans presented a special new way of dealing with rock biographies. Indeed, it was one of the first first peson accounts that presented very personal and intimate episodes in the life of Keith Moon. The book is written with a great deal of love and affection by Dougal Butler who was taking care of of Keith Moon over the years of maximum fame of the Who. While the book emphasizes the extravagant side of Keith Moon and shows how much larger than life he was, it shows at times how unmanageable he was. In this sense it is still the one and only book on Moon that should be bought. I decided to buy it again electronically and it has not at all aged. For anyone interested in the Who, it is indispensable reading.
